| `--no-download` | Skip the download step; only print the result JSON |
| `--no-wait` | Submit and return `request_id` immediately; don't poll |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | Cap the polling wait. Default: model-dependent |
| `--output json` | Print machine-readable JSON for piping (default human-readable) |
| `--quiet` | Suppress progress, keep only the final result line |

content.user_title: Run RunComfy Models from the CLI
content.value_statement: Creative teams and developers need a reliable way to run RunComfy models from automated terminal workflows. This skill explains authentication, schema discovery, job submission, polling, downloads, and safer scripting with the RunComfy CLI.
actual_capabilities: Explains installation and verification paths for the RunComfy CLI.
Guides browser login, token-based CI authentication, and identity checks.
Shows how to run image, video, edit, lip-sync, face swap, and LoRA endpoints.
Documents polling, no-wait jobs, JSON output mode, retry handling, and exit codes.
Describes output downloads, output directories, no-download mode, and model schema lookup.
Lists security boundaries for token storage, endpoint allowlists, and third-party media inputs.
limitations: Requires a separately installed RunComfy CLI before model calls can run.
Requires a valid RunComfy account, token, and enough service credits.
Does not choose safe or legal media rights for user-provided assets.
Model availability, schemas, pricing, and output quality can change on RunComfy.

use_cases.title: Automate Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Run repeatable image or video generation jobs from terminal workflows and save outputs into organized folders.

use_cases.title: Batch Test Model Prompts
use_cases.description: Submit many prompts, capture request IDs, retry transient failures, and compare generated results across models.

use_cases.title: Run Media Jobs In CI
use_cases.description: Use token-based authentication and machine-readable output to connect RunComfy jobs to automation pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RunComfy CLI skill to verify my local setup and explain the next authentication step.

prompt_templates.title: Run One Image Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run a RunComfy text-to-image model, poll until completion, and save outputs to a named folder.

prompt_templates.title: Create Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a safe batch prompt workflow for RunComfy using a prompts file, JSON output, retries, and separate output folders.

prompt_templates.title: Automate No-Wait Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced RunComfy CLI pipeline that submits no-wait jobs, stores request IDs, polls later, handles retryable exit codes, and avoids token exposure.

output_examples.input: User asks to generate a product image with a specific RunComfy model.
output: Identifies required model inputs from the API tab.
Submits the job and reports the downloaded output location.

output_examples.input: User has a list of prompts and wants repeatable batch generation.
output: Builds a batch plan with separate output folders.
Uses safe prompt handling for each request.
Explains retry behavior for timeout and rate-limit errors.

output_examples.input: User needs CI usage without browser login.
output: Recommends token-based authentication through a protected CI secret.
Uses machine-readable output for downstream automation.
Avoids logging token values or generated private URLs.

best_practices: Use verified package manager installation and avoid unattended remote shell installers.
Keep tokens in protected storage and never paste them into prompts, logs, or repositories.
Use explicit output directories and file size expectations for automated runs.
anti_patterns: Do not run model jobs with unreviewed third-party URLs unless the user supplied them for this task.
Do not enable web search unless the task needs current real-world grounding.
Do not mix many model schemas in one command without validating required inputs.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use the RunComfy CLI to authenticate, run model jobs, monitor status, and download generated media.

faq.question: Does it install RunComfy automatically?
faq.answer: It explains installation options. The skill itself is scoped to RunComfy CLI usage after installation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can call terminal tools.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: By default, the CLI downloads files to the current directory. You can set an output directory for each run.

faq.question: How should I handle API tokens?
faq.answer: Use the CLI login flow or protected environment secrets. Never expose tokens in prompts, logs, or source control.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers image generation, video generation, editing, lip sync, face swap, and related RunComfy endpoints.
